_about: The camera and zoom, FIRST OPTION (Track F, exit criterion 7). Read by scripts/world/camera_controller.gd (and far_zoom by scripts/render/fog_layer.gd) through scripts/world/camera_data.gd. EVERY VALUE IS PROPOSED by Track F on 2026-10-09. The design doc leaves zoom range, pixels per world unit and rotation open (Open design details > Camera and scale) and records two of Alex's thoughts this file makes switchable: 'Visual scale on zoom-out is unresolved; may limit zoom-out and have players scroll the map' and 'An interactive overview map the player can set their view from'. ZOOM UNITS: Camera2D zoom, screen px per MAP px (the map is drawn in map px = metres x data/terrain/terrain.json scale.px_per_m: 2 is Alex's demo baseline and it is a live knob, 1-4). Zoom is in map px on purpose: the render's detail (trees, linework) is drawn in map px at every scale, so a zoom limit about legibility holds at any px_per_m; the zoom-out limit 'fit_map' and every margin in metres follow the scale. The arithmetic in the reasons is at 2 px/m and a 1280 x 720 view; nothing in code assumes either. No rotation: north stays up.

min._reason: 'fit_map': the hard zoom-out limit is the whole map in the view (times fit_margin), whatever the map size and px_per_m -- with far_zoom.mode 'overview_topo' the far view IS the overview map. At 2 px/m a 5,000 m map in 720 px is zoom 0.072 (0.068 with the margin; 0.034 at 4 px/m). A number is a fixed limit

fit_margin._reason: a little paper around the map at the fit_map limit

max._reason: PROPOSED 3.0 by builder CAM, 2026-10-11 (decision playtest-3, tank_zoom: Alex, 'You need to be able to zoom in further, they are too small'). Was 2.0 (two screen px per map px: the ink linework is drawn for zoom 1, the prototype's scale, so past 2 the baked map is magnified). A tank is drawn at 1.33 x the map's scale in Hold the bridge (view.plane_px 24 over the 9 m plane reference at 2 px/m), so its hull is about 18 px long per unit of zoom (measured on the native shot at 3.0: 54 px, and its gun 15 px more): 36 px at the old closest zoom 2.0, 54 px at 3.0 (about 69 px with its gun), 63 px at 3.5, 72 px at 4.0, and about 10 px at the opening zoom 0.12. The map is baked at one texel per map px, so at 3.0 each texel is three screen px: the trees' and the ground's inked edges are soft (bilinear, not blocky: shots tmp/cam/shots/z3_mid.png, z4_mid.png); what is drawn live or baked at the screen scale (units, the bridge, labels, the map's border band) stays crisp. 3.5 and 4.0 were looked at: softer each step. The bake itself was not changed

start._reason: a planning view: at 2 px/m it is 1,830 x 1,030 m, a light fighter's turn at cruise (5 s x 100 m/s = 500 m) with room for the heavy fighter's 825 m at top speed, and trees are still 13 px

wheel_step._reason: zoom factor per mouse wheel notch, in toward the cursor and out about the centre of the map area (Alex, decision zoom-anchors; the step is proposed): 12 notches from planning zoom to the whole map at 2 px/m

keys_step_per_s._reason: zoom factor per second while a zoom key is held (zoom_in / zoom_out keys)

keys_px_per_s._reason: SCREEN px per second while a pan key is held, so a key pan feels the same at every zoom

drag_buttons._reason: buttons that drag the map anywhere. Alex, 2026-10-11 (decision pan-right-drag-off): the right button no longer pans -- it was [middle, right]; right-click is the point target alone. The left button is the planner's and the roster's (Track U); a left drag on EMPTY map pans through left_drag_slop_px below

left_drag_slop_px._reason: Alex, decision pan-left-drag: a LEFT drag on empty map pans (a press Track U's interface does not use: no unit, step handle, fan or bomb cone under it -- UnitUI.empty_map_press -> CameraController.begin_grab). This is how far the pointer must move from the press before the pan starts (screen px), so a click on empty map stays a click; the pan then catches up and the point pressed stays under the pointer. 4: the right-click target's slop (ui.json target.right_click.slop_px); Godot's gui_drag_threshold is 10, Windows' SM_CXDRAG 4, Mapbox's clickTolerance 3

keys._reason: physical key names (OS.find_keycode_from_string); WASD and arrows pan, Q/E and -/= zoom about the centre of the map area (the view less the HUD insets)

trackpad_px_per_unit._reason: screen px a trackpad two-finger pan moves per unit of its gesture delta

edge_overscroll_m._reason: THE VIEW STOPS AT THE MAP'S EDGE (Alex, 2026-10-11, decision pan-stops-at-edge: keep the zoom-out limit at fit_map and stop panning past the edge): the free area (the view less the HUD insets) shows at most this many metres past the map's edge, at every zoom but the full zoom-out, where the whole map is centred (and the strips beside it, from the window's shape, show the map's border: data/view/map_border.json). PROPOSED 100 m: the border's band at the planning zoom (70 px at 0.35, 200 px at zoom 1 at 2 px/m). It replaced pan.map_margin_m (1000 m, how far the view CENTRE could go past the edge, so a plane that had left the map could still be looked at): a plane more than this beyond the edge is now out of reach of the camera

smoothing_per_s._reason: follow-selected-unit eases the view toward the unit at this rate (exponential; 0 snaps). 8/s closes 90% of a gap in about 0.3 s

break_on_pan._reason: a manual pan or drag stops following, so the player can look away from a moving unit

break_on_zoom._reason: PROPOSED by builder CAM, 2026-10-11 (decision playtest-3, zoom_judder: 'like there's two systems fighting each other for deciding the view'). A zoom the player makes (wheel, pinch, zoom keys) that changes the zoom stops following, as a pan does. Why: following puts the unit at the centre of the map area every frame, a wheel zoom keeps the point under the cursor; with both on, each notch moved the view one way and the follow eased it back (measured, tmp/cam/probe_follow.csv: ten notches at a fixed cursor ended with the point 826 px from it, the camera moving backwards between notches). Alex's decided zoom (in toward the cursor, out about the centre) cannot hold under a follow, so the follow is the one that gives way. false brings back the old behaviour (the fight). The other way to settle it, PROPOSED alternative not built: keep following through a zoom and zoom about the followed unit

margin_px._reason: SCREEN px kept clear around a framed plan, so the end points and their markers are not under the window edge

max_zoom._reason: frame-this-plan never zooms in past the prototype's scale, even for a one-step plan

insets_px._reason: screen space the HUD covers, left out of framing. 0 here; Track A sets the roster sidebar's width (set_insets) when it mounts the interface

mode._reason: Alex 2026-10-09 accepted the lead's fog recommendation (the whole map as the contour overview when zoomed out). Was proposed: WHAT THE VIEW DOES AT FAR ZOOM (the design doc leaves it open; its proposal under UI and HUD is this one). 'overview_topo': below topo_below_zoom the topographic map shows everywhere -- the fog's map, the vision edges drawn on it -- so ink detail never shrinks into noise and the far view doubles as the overview map; the map view need not bake the full render out there. 'full_render': the full render at every zoom, and the hard zoom-out limit becomes full_render_min_zoom (Alex: 'may limit zoom-out and have players scroll the map')

topo_below_zoom._reason: fully topographic at or below this zoom: a 38 px canopy is 4 px -- the render has turned to texture. At 2 px/m the view is then 5,800 x 3,270 m, the whole map's width: in practice 'zoomed out to the map'. With 1,500 m sight a whole vision circle (3,000 px across at 2 px/m) first fits a 720 px view at zoom 0.12, so the circles come into view as the overview fades in

full_above_zoom._reason: fully the full render at or above this zoom (trees 6 px; at 2 px/m a 4,000 x 2,250 m view); between the two the topographic map fades in

full_render_min_zoom._reason: the zoom-out limit when mode is 'full_render', the legibility floor (trees 4.5 px): at 2 px/m a 5,330 x 3,000 m view, nearly the whole map; at 4 px/m half of it, and the player scrolls for the rest
